React's current stable documentation line is 19.3, verified at https://react.dev/versions and https://react.dev/blog/2026/09/09/react-19-3. There is no single React package version shared by both routers: https://nextjs.org/docs explains that the App Router uses bundled React Canary builds, while the Pages Router uses the project's installed React. The official Next.js 16.3.8 tagged manifest at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel/next.js/v16.3.8/package.json pins react-builtin and react-dom-builtin to 19.3.0-canary-cbb046ab-20260731. This bundled runtime identifier is distinct from the public stable React release. Opened every distinct official URL in this batch's card source fields. Additional pages opened for whole-deck planning: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/caching; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/server-actions; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/forms; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/client-side-data-fetching/swr; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag; https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag; https://react.dev/reference/react/cache; https://react.dev/reference/react/startTransition. All eight requested sections remain supported. The current caching and revalidating getting-started pages describe Cache Components enabled; the previous-model guide describes the flag-disabled model. Cache Components is opt-in in Next.js 16. Its migration guide states that legacy route-level dynamic, revalidate and fetchCache configuration is replaced in the enabled model. The Pages Router remains supported. The Next.js 14-to-15 caching-default comparison is historical, rather than current-version guidance. The former experimental PPR configuration is removed; Partial Prerendering belongs to the Cache Components model. Single-argument revalidateTag usage is deprecated.

cards.statement: App Router layouts and pages are Server Components by default.
cards.explanation: Route-level UI starts in the server component graph until a client boundary is explicitly introduced.

cards.statement: The 'use client' boundary includes modules imported by the marked file.
cards.explanation: A file marked with use client brings its imported dependencies into the client module graph as well.

cards.statement: A Server Component passed as children can keep server execution inside a Client Component.
cards.explanation: The receiving Client Component places the supplied rendered output; it does not import or execute the Server Component implementation.

cards.statement: A Server Component can pass a Date object as a prop to a Client Component.
cards.explanation: React includes Date among the built-in types its server-to-client serialization supports.

cards.statement: Using server-only in a plain data module makes a Client Component import fail at build time.
cards.explanation: The server-only marker makes Next.js reject a regular client-graph import of that data module during the build.

cards.statement: A Server Component can render an HTML details element that opens through built-in browser behavior.
cards.explanation: The browser implements the disclosure interaction for details, so a Server Component can provide that markup directly.

cards.statement: A Server Component can pass an ordinary onClick callback to a Client Component.
cards.explanation: A plain event-handler function is an unsupported prop at the server-to-client boundary; define that callback in client code.
cards.misconception: Ordinary event-handler closures can be serialized as client props.

cards.statement: A Server Component can read React context from a wrapping Client Component provider.
cards.explanation: Client context is consumed by Client Components. A provider surrounding Server Component output does not make that context readable during the server render.
cards.misconception: An enclosing client provider makes context available to Server Components.

cards.statement: Adding 'use server' to a component file declares its exports as Server Components.
cards.explanation: The use server directive identifies Server Functions. Server Components have no corresponding declaration directive.
cards.misconception: The use server directive is the component-level counterpart of use client.

cards.statement: React accepts custom class instances as props passed from Server Components to Client Components.
cards.explanation: Instances of application-defined classes are outside React's supported server-to-client prop types, even when their fields look serializable.
cards.misconception: An object with simple fields is serializable regardless of its custom prototype.

cards.statement: A Server Component can manage a controlled input with useState.
cards.explanation: Interactive state managed with useState belongs in a Client Component rather than a Server Component.
cards.misconception: Server Components can retain local interactive state with useState.

cards.statement: An async function is a supported way to define a Client Component.
cards.explanation: React rejects async Client Component functions. Keep the Client Component function synchronous.
cards.misconception: The async component function pattern works in Client Components.

cards.statement: The RSC Payload is the HTML document that the browser displays during the initial page visit.
cards.explanation: The RSC Payload is serialized React tree data, a different representation from HTML markup.
cards.misconception: The RSC Payload and the HTML response are the same representation.

cards.statement: The RSC Payload includes references to the JavaScript files for Client Components.
cards.explanation: References in the RSC Payload identify the JavaScript files associated with its Client Component positions.

cards.statement: On a direct visit, a Client Component can render on the server before browser hydration.
cards.explanation: Next.js can execute Client Components to generate the initial HTML before their browser-side hydration.

cards.statement: On later client-side navigations, Next.js renders Client Components into HTML on the server.
cards.explanation: For client-side navigation, Client Components render in the browser instead of receiving newly server-rendered HTML.
cards.misconception: Client-side navigation repeats the initial server HTML pass for Client Components.

cards.statement: React uses an incoming RSC Payload to reconcile the active component tree.
cards.explanation: An incoming RSC Payload describes rendered component output that React reconciles into the active UI.

cards.statement: Hydration replaces the server-rendered DOM with a newly created page.
cards.explanation: Hydration connects React to the existing server-generated DOM and attaches the behavior needed for interaction.
cards.misconception: Hydration rebuilds the document instead of adopting the existing markup.

cards.statement: hydrateRoot expects the initial browser render to match the server-rendered content.
cards.explanation: The initial client result should agree with the existing server markup; hydration mismatches indicate bugs to fix.

cards.statement: suppressHydrationWarning repairs mismatched text during hydration.
cards.explanation: suppressHydrationWarning silences a mismatch warning; React does not repair the mismatched text as part of that hydration.
cards.misconception: Suppressing a hydration warning also corrects the differing text.

cards.statement: Calling root.render before hydration finishes preserves the existing server-rendered HTML.
cards.explanation: An early root.render call discards the root's server HTML and switches the root to client rendering.
cards.misconception: A render call during hydration updates the tree while retaining the server HTML.

cards.statement: useEffect callbacks execute on the server while Next.js renders a page for its first browser visit.
cards.explanation: Effects execute on the client. Generating HTML on the server does not execute a component's useEffect callback.
cards.misconception: Server rendering runs Effects along with the component render function.

cards.statement: Shared layouts preserve their state during client-side navigation between their child routes.
cards.explanation: During navigation, the shared layout stays mounted while its child route content changes, preserving its state.

cards.statement: Next.js can fetch a destination's RSC Payload before the user navigates to that route.
cards.explanation: Prefetching retrieves a destination's RSC Payload ahead of navigation so the router can reuse that work.

cards.statement: On an initial render, reading a pending Promise with use activates the nearest Suspense fallback.
cards.explanation: An initial render that reads an unresolved Promise with use suspends at the closest surrounding Suspense boundary.

cards.statement: Nested Suspense boundaries can reveal an outer section while deeper content is still loading.
cards.explanation: Nested Suspense boundaries let a ready outer section display while an inner section remains on its fallback.

cards.statement: Components sharing one nearest Suspense boundary reveal together when their initial content is ready.
cards.explanation: A shared Suspense boundary treats the initial content it controls as a coordinated reveal unit.

cards.statement: Suspense detects a fetch started inside useEffect and shows its fallback while that request runs.
cards.explanation: A request started in an Effect does not itself activate Suspense; suspension requires a supported render-time resource.
cards.misconception: Any pending fetch automatically engages the surrounding Suspense boundary.

cards.statement: React preserves a component's state across a suspension that happens before its first mount.
cards.explanation: React retries a tree that suspended before its first mount from scratch, rather than retaining that unfinished render's state.
cards.misconception: A suspended initial render retains component state for the eventual mount.

cards.statement: A Transition replaces revealed content with a fallback when the same Suspense boundary suspends again.
cards.explanation: A Transition keeps already revealed content visible when its update suspends, rather than replacing it with a loading fallback.
cards.misconception: Transition updates hide already revealed content whenever new work suspends.

cards.statement: A streamed HTML shell can include a Suspense fallback while that boundary's content is pending.
cards.explanation: React can send a Suspense fallback in the initial HTML shell before the pending content finishes rendering.

cards.statement: Sibling Suspense boundaries stream their completed content in component-tree order.
cards.explanation: Independent sibling Suspense boundaries can stream as their work finishes; source order does not prescribe completion order.
cards.misconception: An earlier sibling boundary has priority over a later boundary that is ready sooner.

cards.statement: Server-rendered page sections can arrive in chunks within the same HTTP response.
cards.explanation: The document response can remain open as the server sends additional rendered content.

cards.statement: Next.js can change the HTTP status code after a streamed response starts sending its body.
cards.explanation: Once the response body starts streaming, its status and headers are committed; later UI outcomes cannot rewrite that HTTP status.
cards.misconception: A later rendering result can replace the status of an in-progress HTTP response.

cards.statement: A segment's loading.js fallback covers an await in that same segment's enclosing layout.
cards.explanation: The boundary created by loading.js sits inside its segment's layout, leaving that layout's own await outside the fallback's coverage.
cards.misconception: The segment loading boundary surrounds its own enclosing layout.

cards.statement: A shared layout can stay interactive while loading.js displays feedback for the incoming route.
cards.explanation: During navigation, loading.js can show a loading view while the shared layout continues responding to interaction.

cards.statement: In the Pages Router, getStaticProps supplies props for build-time prerendering in production.
cards.explanation: The production build resolves getStaticProps before emitting the Pages Router page's initial static HTML.

cards.statement: In the Pages Router, getServerSideProps can use request-time data to render a page.
cards.explanation: getServerSideProps runs while Next.js handles a page request, so it can read request-specific inputs.

cards.statement: In the Pages Router, a nested UI component can export getStaticProps to load its own data.
cards.explanation: Next.js invokes getStaticProps as a page-level export, not as a loader exported by an arbitrary nested UI component.
cards.misconception: Each nested UI component can register its own getStaticProps loader.

cards.statement: In the Pages Router, getStaticPaths configures the paths for a page using getServerSideProps.
cards.explanation: getStaticPaths is paired with getStaticProps on a dynamic page, rather than with getServerSideProps.
cards.misconception: getStaticPaths configures dynamic paths for request-time getServerSideProps pages.

cards.statement: In the Pages Router, fallback: false returns a 404 for a path omitted from getStaticPaths.
cards.explanation: With getStaticPaths and fallback: false, Next.js serves 404 for paths outside the generated set.

cards.statement: In the Pages Router, fallback: 'blocking' shows a loading fallback while generating a new path.
cards.explanation: With fallback: 'blocking', the initial request for a new path waits for generated HTML instead of receiving a loading fallback.
cards.misconception: The blocking fallback mode displays a loading UI while a new path is generated.

cards.statement: In the Pages Router, App.getInitialProps preserves Automatic Static Optimization on otherwise eligible pages.
cards.explanation: A custom App using getInitialProps turns off automatic optimization for pages that would otherwise rely on it.
cards.misconception: Custom App data loading leaves automatic page optimization unchanged.

cards.statement: In the Pages Router, an automatically optimized page can receive query values in a post-hydration update.
cards.explanation: An automatically optimized Pages Router page can rerender after hydration when Next.js supplies its query values.

cards.statement: In Next.js 16 with cacheComponents off, a dynamic URL segment forces request-time rendering.
cards.explanation: With Cache Components disabled, generateStaticParams can provide values that let Next.js prerender a dynamic URL segment.
cards.misconception: A dynamic URL pattern implies dynamic rendering rather than prerendering.
cards.volatilityNote: Rendering decisions are scoped to the previous caching model; Cache Components changes that model.

cards.statement: In Next.js 16 with cacheComponents off and default route config, reading cookies() makes a page dynamic.
cards.explanation: In the previous model's automatic mode, cookies() needs incoming request data and opts the page into request-time rendering.
cards.appliesTo: Next.js 16 with cacheComponents: false and default route config
cards.volatilityNote: The route-wide effect applies to the previous model and depends on route configuration.

cards.statement: In Next.js 16 with cacheComponents off, useSearchParams client-renders static UI above the nearest Suspense boundary.
cards.explanation: On a prerendered route, useSearchParams moves rendering to the client up to the nearest Suspense boundary; UI above it can stay prerendered.
cards.misconception: useSearchParams forces client rendering above the nearest enclosing Suspense boundary.
cards.volatilityNote: This prerendering rule is pinned to the previous caching model and the current hook contract.

cards.statement: Awaiting connection() in a Server Component excludes rendering below that call from prerendering.
cards.explanation: connection() waits for an incoming request before the subsequent rendering continues.
